'''Anthony A. Armstrong''' (born March 29, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Texas A&M Buffaloes football|West Texas A&M Buffaloes]] and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in 2008.

He was also a member of the [[Washington Redskins]] and [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. Before joining the NFL, Armstrong was a member of the [[Dallas Desperados]] of the [[Arena Football League]] and the [[Odessa Roughnecks]] of the [[Intense Football League]].

==Early life==
Armstrong was born on March 29, 1983, in [[Greencastle, Indiana]].  His mother, Gwen Armstrong, worked as an Administration Manager at [[IBM]] and his father, Thomas Armstrong, died when Anthony was 2 days short of 6 years old.<ref>{{cite news|last=Maese|first=Rick|title=After a long and uncertain journey, rookie wide receiver Anthony Armstrong is a bright spot for the Washington Redskins|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2011/01/01/AR2011010102467.html|work=[[The Washington Post]]|accessdate=March 10, 2011|date=January 2, 2011}}</ref> Anthony is a middle child of 4. He has a brother named Courtney Lee and two sisters, Catrina Scott and  Ashley Armstrong  . When Anthony was a teenager, he played [[high school football]] at [[Newman Smith High School]].  During his senior season, he had 11 receptions for 250 yards and three touchdowns<ref name=redskins>{{cite web | work=[[Washington Redskins]] | url=http://www.redskins.com/team/roster/Anthony-Armstrong/12543fae-3985-426c-b8ae-e216316c0c4d | title=Anthony Armstrong's Washington Redskins bio | accessdate=October 17, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513221609/http://www.redskins.com/team/roster/anthony-armstrong/12543fae-3985-426c-b8ae-e216316c0c4d/ | archive-date=May 13, 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and was named to the All-Metrocrest second-team.<ref name=dallas>{{cite web|work=[[Dallas Desperados]] |url=http://www.dallasdesperados.com/dd_player_armstrong_anthony.cfm |title=Anthony Armstrong's Dallas Desperados bio |accessdate=October 17, 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100507024755/http://www.dallasdesperados.com/dd_player_armstrong_anthony.cfm |archivedate=May 7, 2010 }}</ref>  He also lettered twice as a member of the [[track and field]] team<ref name=redskins /> and competed in the [[100 metres|100-meter dash]].<ref name=dallas />

==College career==
Armstrong attended and played [[college football]] at [[West Texas A&M University]], a [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] school in [[Canyon, Texas]].  As a freshman, he played in ten games and had 165 yards and one touchdown on 13 catches.  The following season, he played in ten games and recorded 24 receptions for 256 yards.<ref name=redskins />  As a junior, Armstrong started all 11 games and caught 54 passes for 740 yards and four touchdowns.  He was named the [[Lone Star Conference|LSC South]] Receiver of the Year and earned first-team All-LSC South honors.<ref name=redskins />  In his final college season, Armstrong was named second-team All-LSC as a senior after leading the team with 54 catches for 607 yards and four touchdowns.  He finished his four-year letterman career as West Texas A&M's fourth leading receiver with 145 receptions for 1,768 yards and nine touchdowns.<ref name=redskins />

Armstrong graduated from West Texas A&M with a degree in marketing.<ref name=redskins />

==Arena and Indoor football career==
Armstrong was signed by the [[West Texas Roughnecks|Odessa Roughnecks]] of the [[Intense Football League]] in 2006.  In 13 games for the Roughnecks, he had 55 receptions for 760 yards and 18 touchdowns<ref name=redskins /> and returned seven kickoffs for 166 yards and a touchdown.<ref name=dallas />  He was the team's second leading rusher and rushed four times for 39 yards and three touchdowns.  Armstrong also had eight tackles, two pass breakups and a [[fumble]] recovery on defense.<ref name=dallas />  His best game was against the [[Louisiana Swashbucklers]] on July 1, 2006, during which he registered 11 receptions for 157 yards and three touchdowns.  The Roughnecks won the IFL championship during Armstrong's only season on the team.<ref name=odessa>{{cite web | work=[[Indoor Football League]] | url=http://www.goifl.com/news/index.html?article_id=2030 | title=Former Roughnecks WR Anthony Armstrong Signs to Washington Redskins Practice Squad | accessdate=October 17, 2010 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124072005/http://goifl.com/news/index.html?article_id=2030 | archivedate=November 24, 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2007, Armstrong joined the [[Dallas Desperados]] of the [[Arena Football League]] as a practice squad member and was signed to active roster on March 25, 2007.  He made his AFL debut against the [[Austin Wranglers]] on March 31, 2007, where he recovered an [[onside kick]] and returned it 40 yards for the game-winning touchdown.<ref name=dallas />  Armstrong was placed on the Reserve/Injured list with a hamstring injury on May 2 and missed the remainder of the season, after recording ten catches for 126 yards and two touchdowns in four games.<ref name=redskins />  He played the entire 2008 season with the Desperados and posted 85 catches for 1,148 yards and 18 touchdowns.  He additionally returned seven kickoffs for 31 yards helping the team compile a 12–4 regular season record and a berth to the AFL playoffs.<ref name=odessa />

==National Football League career==

===Miami Dolphins===
After the Arena Football League season, Armstrong was signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]]' practice squad as an [[unrestricted free agent]] on July 25, 2008.<ref name=redskins />  He stayed on the practice squad the entire season and the 2009 preseason, but was waived August 29, 2009.

===Washington Redskins===

====2009 season====
Armstrong signed with the [[Washington Redskins]] on October 21, 2009, and spent the final 10 weeks on the Redskins' practice squad.<ref name=redskins />

====2010 season====
Armstrong made his first regular season NFL career catch for 11 yards on September 12, 2010, in a 13–7 win over the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and soon emerged as one of the Redskins' primary deep threats.  He recorded a career long 76-yard reception against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on November 15, 2010, finishing fourth among all receivers with 7 receptions of 40 yards or more for the 2010–2011 season. Among receivers with at least 20 receptions over the season, Armstrong finished third with 19.8 yards/catch.

====2011 season====
In Week 1 against the [[New York Giants]], Armstrong made his first touchdown of the [[2011 NFL season|2011 season]].<ref name="z180">{{cite web | last=Prada | first=Mike | title=Giants Vs. Redskins Score Update: Anthony Armstrong Touchdown Ties Score At 14 | website=SB Nation DC | date=2011-09-11 | url=https://dc.sbnation.com/washington-redskins/2011/9/11/2418960/giants-vs-redskins-score-update-halftime-anthony-armstrong | access-date=2024-11-28}}</ref>
He would not get another touchdown until Week 12 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], where he caught a 50-yard touchdown pass from [[Rex Grossman]] helping to end the Redskins' six-game losing streak.<ref>{{cite news | work=WashingtonPost.com | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sportsredskins/anthony-armstrong-takes-advantage-of-rare-opportunity-with-the-redskins/2011/11/27/gIQAXsHY3N_story.html | title=Anthony Armstrong takes advantage of rare opportunity with the Redskins | accessdate=November 27, 2011 | first=Rick | last=Maese | date=November 28, 2011 | archive-date=March 12, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312060144/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sportsredskins/anthony-armstrong-takes-advantage-of-rare-opportunity-with-the-redskins/2011/11/27/gIQAXsHY3N_story.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2012 season====
The Redskins released Armstrong on August 31, 2012, for final roster cuts before the start of the [[2012 NFL season|2012 season]] and he was picked up by the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite news| work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2012/08/31/redskins-release-wr-anthony-armstrong/|title=Redskins release WR Anthony Armstrong|last=Jones|first=Mike|date=August 31, 2012|accessdate=August 31, 2012}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins (second stint)===
On September 1, 2012, Armstrong was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/dolphins-blog/sfl-miami-dolphins-claim-receiver-anthony-armstrong-20120901,0,5302987.story |title=Miami Dolphins claim receiver Anthony Armstrong, release Steve Slaton |access-date=September 1, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203080705/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/dolphins-blog/sfl-miami-dolphins-claim-receiver-anthony-armstrong-20120901,0,5302987.story |archive-date=February 3, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived on October 30.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Armstrong was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on October 31, 2012. He was released by the team on November 12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2012 |title=Jaguars awarded WR Anthony Armstrong off waivers |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-awarded-wr-anthony-armstrong-off-waivers-8711925 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
After working out with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on November 21, 2012, the team signed Armstrong on November 26.<ref>{{cite news|last=Boren|first=Cindy|title=Anthony Armstrong signs with Dallas Cowboys|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2012/11/26/anthony-armstrong-signs-with-dallas-cowboys/?wprss=rss_sports|work=[[The Washington Post]]|date=November 26, 2012|accessdate=November 26, 2012}}</ref>  He was released on December 22.<ref>{{cite news|last=Burch|first=Jimmy|title=Cowboys release WR Armstrong, sign OL Leary to active roster|url=http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/cowboys/2012/12/cowboys-release-wr-armstrong-sign-ol-leary-to-active-roster.html|work=[[Star-Telegram]]|date=December 22, 2012|accessdate=December 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208051828/http://sportsblogs.star-telegram.com/cowboys/2012/12/cowboys-release-wr-armstrong-sign-ol-leary-to-active-roster.html|archive-date=December 8, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 7, 2013, Armstrong signed a one-year, $630,000 contract. He was released on March 27. On April 3, Armstrong re-signed with the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/04/03/anthony-armstrong-re-signing-with-cowboys/|title=Anthony Armstrong re-signing with Cowboys|first=Mike|last=Wilkening|date=April 3, 2013|accessdate=April 3, 2013}}</ref> He was released by the team on August 31.<ref name="v941">{{cite web | last=Watkins | first=Calvin | title=Anthony Armstrong is released | website=ESPN.com | date=2013-08-30 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4713842/anthony-armstrong-is-released | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Armstrong signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] on May 19, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns add seven to roster|url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-add-seven-to-roster-/1292e4c8-7a0f-4b14-98e2-c55fbfa9405b|publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com|accessdate=May 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520020258/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-add-seven-to-roster-/1292e4c8-7a0f-4b14-98e2-c55fbfa9405b|archive-date=May 20, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
He was released by the team on August 25.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-make-roster-moves/bc504c27-6da2-4700-9eb0-77990af1e3ae |title=Browns make roster moves |access-date=August 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507085914/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-make-roster-moves/bc504c27-6da2-4700-9eb0-77990af1e3ae |archive-date=May 7, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Andrew Steven Levitre''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ə|ˈ|v|iː|t|r|i}} {{respell|lə|VEE|tree}}; born May 15, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers]] and was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the second round of the [[2009 NFL draft]]. He also played in the NFL for the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Atlanta Falcons]].

==Early life==
Levitre played [[high school football]] at [[San Lorenzo Valley High School]] in [[Felton, California]], where he was a two-way lineman.<ref name="d424">{{cite web | title=Local Roundup: Santa Cruz’s Levitre placed on IR, will miss NFL playoffs | website=Santa Cruz Sentinel | date=2018-01-06 | url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2018/01/06/local-roundup-santa-cruzs-levitre-placed-on-ir-will-miss-nfl-playoffs/ | access-date=2024-11-28}}</ref> In his [[Eleventh grade|junior]] season, he recorded 47 tackles, two [[quarterback sacks]] and two fumble recoveries. He added more than 60 tackles and three sacks in his [[Twelfth grade|senior]] year.

Considered only a two-star recruit by both ''[[Rivals.com]]'' and ''[[Scout.com]]'',<ref name="Rivals Recruiting Profile">{{Cite web |title=Andy Levitre Recruiting Profile |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Andy-Levitre-21697 |access-date=November 28, 2009 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref><ref name="Scout Recruiting Profile">{{Cite web |title=Andy Levitre Recruiting Profile |url=http://recruiting.scout.com/a.z?s=73&p=8&c=1&nid=806321 |access-date=November 28, 2009 |website=Scout.com}}</ref> Levitre was not ranked among the nation's top offensive line prospects in 2004. He chose Oregon State over [[Louisiana State University|LSU]], [[Fresno State University|Fresno State]], and [[University of Arizona|Arizona]],<ref name="Eggers">{{Cite web |last=Eggers |first=Kerry |date=December 11, 2008 |title=Credits pile up for OSU's top blocker |url=http://www.osubeavers.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/030509abi.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120301010506/http://www.osubeavers.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/030509abi.html |archive-date=March 1, 2012 |website=Portland Tribune}}</ref> where his older brother, Erick, played [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] (2002–2006).

==College career==
Levitre [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] in 2004, and played in all 11 games as a redshirt-freshman in 2005, while starting against [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]]. In his sophomore season, he started in game four of the season after senior starter Josh Linehan injured a knee in game three against [[Idaho Vandals football|Idaho]]. Levitre earned Pac-10 Honorable Mention as a player and academically.

During his junior year, Levitre started every game at either right or left tackle, and earned Pac-10 Conference second-team honors as selected by the coaches. For his senior season he was named to the 2008 [[Outland Trophy]] watch list, and started all 13 games at left tackle. He registered a career-high 91 knockdowns and 14 touchdown-resulting blocks and was earned All-American status by the [[American Football Coaches Association]] and ''[[Pro Football Weekly]]''. He was considered the most-decorated Beaver offensive lineman since [[John Didion]], a consensus All-America choice in the late 1960s.<ref name="Eggers" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Levitre College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits  |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andy-levitre-1.html |access-date=January 7, 2018 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Alongside [[Duke Robinson]] and [[T. J. Lang]], Levitre was considered one of the best guards available in the [[2009 NFL draft]].<ref name="CBS center ranking">{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2009 |title=NFL Draft – 2009 OG Draft Prospects |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/prospectrankings/TSX/2009_OG |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> He has been compared to [[Todd Herremans]] by ''The Sporting News'',<ref name="TSNprofile">{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2009 |title=Pro Football War Room: Andy Levitre |url=http://warroom.sportingnews.com/nfl/draft/2009/players/8440.html |website=SportingNews.com}}</ref> and to [[Josh Beekman]] by ''CBS Sports''.<ref name="CBS draft profile">{{Cite web |title=Andy Levitre Draft Profile |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/504719 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
[[File:Andy Levitre.JPG|175px|thumbnail|right|Levitre in 2011.]]
Levitre was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] with the 51st pick overall in the second round of the [[2009 NFL draft]], and was the first college guard drafted.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=January 7, 2018 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He is the sixth selection from Oregon State in Bills history, the first since [[Keith Ellison (American football)|Keith Ellison]] in [[2006 NFL draft|2006]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oregon St. Drafted Players/Alumni |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/oregonst/drafted.htm |access-date=January 7, 2018 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Counted on to start at left guard, Levitre joined a completely retooled offensive line that was expected to feature two rookie starters—him, and first round pick [[Eric Wood]] at right guard—and no players returning at the same position. He started all 16 games in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 26, 2010 |title=Inside The Bills |url=http://blogs.buffalobills.com/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110123191806/http://blogs.buffalobills.com/ |archive-date=January 23, 2011 |access-date=December 30, 2010 |publisher=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

On January 15, 2010, Levitre was named to the 2009 NFL All-Rookie team along with teammate [[Jairus Byrd]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 14, 2010 |title=2009 NFL All-Rookie Team – NFL |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/article/2010-01-14/sporting-news-2009-nfl-all-rookie-team |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100620095414/http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/article/2010-01-14/sporting-news-2009-nfl-all-rookie-team |archive-date=June 20, 2010 |access-date=December 30, 2010 |publisher=Sporting News}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 12, 2013, Levitre reached a six-year $46.8 million deal with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web | last1=Wyatt | first1=Jim | title=Titans lure Andy Levitre with 6-year, $46.8 million deal | website=USA TODAY | date=2013-03-12 | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2013/03/12/tennessee-titans-andy-levitre/1982981/#:~:text=Slow%20to%20move%20in%20previous,-year%2C%20%2446.8%20million%20contract. | access-date=2025-10-11}}</ref> Levitre underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in January 2013 and still felt knee soreness just days after signing for the team.<ref name="j210">{{cite web | last=Wesseling | first=Chris | title=Andy Levitre out for Tennessee Titans after surgery | website=NFL.com | date=2013-05-31 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/andy-levitre-out-for-tennessee-titans-after-surgery-0ap1000000208338 | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On September 4, 2015, the Titans traded Levitre to the [[Atlanta Falcons]] for a 2016 sixth round draft pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr, Conor |date=September 4, 2015 |title=Titans trade Andy Levitre to Atlanta Falcons |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/titans-trade-andy-levitre-to-atlanta-falcons-0ap3000000521868 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

In the 2016 season, Levitre and the Falcons reached [[Super Bowl LI]], where they faced the [[2016 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] on February 5, 2017. In the Super Bowl, the Falcons fell in a 34–28 overtime defeat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LI – New England Patriots vs. Atlanta Falcons – February 5th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201702050atl.htm |access-date=August 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

In 2017, Levitre started the first 12 games of the season at left guard before suffering a triceps injury. He missed the next three games before returning in Week 17 against the Carolina Panthers, where he aggravated the injury. He was placed on injured reserve on January 2, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conway, Kelsey |date=January 2, 2018 |title=Falcons place starting left guard Andy Levitre on injured reserve list |url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/article-1/Falcons-place-starting-left-guard-Andy-Levitre-on-injured-reserve-list/65f08e00-5eef-4a68-96f0-5d88ed35c71b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103193337/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/article-1/Falcons-place-starting-left-guard-Andy-Levitre-on-injured-reserve-list/65f08e00-5eef-4a68-96f0-5d88ed35c71b |archive-date=January 3, 2018 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref>

On September 18, 2018, Levitre was placed on injured reserve after suffering a torn triceps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden, Will |date=September 18, 2018 |title=Falcons place Andy Levitre on injured reserve, sign Zac Kerin |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-place-andy-levitre-on-injured-reserve-sign-zac-kerin |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref>

On May 14, 2019, Levitre announced his retirement from the NFL after 10 seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope, Herbie |date=May 14, 2019 |title=Andy Levitre announces retirement after 10 seasons |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/andy-levitre-announces-retirement-after-10-seasons-0ap3000001030771 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

By protecting quarterback [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] at right tackle, he helped pave the way for the Eagles' 5,924 yards in total offense. Castonzo subsequently received All-ACC Freshman honors by ''[[The Sporting News]]'' and Freshman All-American honors by the ''[[Football Writers Association of America]]''.{{Citation |title=AON Insurance/FWAA Freshman All-America Team 2007 |date=January 7, 2008 |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2007/allamerica080107.html |publisher=FWAA}} Prior to his sophomore season, Castonzo made the move from right tackle to left tackle where he started all 14 games in 2008. Boston College ranked 25th in the country in tackles for a loss allowed (4.77) and 49th in sacks allowed (1.69). Castonzo earned a ''[[College Football News]]'' All-Sophomore First-team selection.{{Citation |last=Cirminiello |first=Richard |title=2008 CFN All-Sophomore Team |date=December 11, 2008 |url=http://cfn.scout.com/2/820628.html |work=College Football News |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222045256/http://cfn.scout.com/2/820628.html |access-date=August 4, 2009 |archive-date=February 22, 2012 |url-status=dead}} In 2009, Castonzo was listed at No. 9 on ''[[Rivals.com]]′s'' preseason offensive tackle power ranking.{{Citation |last=Buchanan |first=Olin |title=Preseason offensive tackle power rankings |date=August 22, 2009 |url=http://rivals100.rivals.com/content.asp?cid=978914 |work=Rivals.com |last2=Dienhart |first2=Tom |last3=Fox |first3=David |last4=Huguenin |first4=Mike |last5=Megargee |first5=Steve |access-date=September 1, 2009 |archive-date=March 24, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324093700/https://rivals100.rivals.com/content.asp?cid=978914 |url-status=dead }} Following a productive junior season, Castonzo was selected 2009 First-team All-Atlantic Coast Conference as voted on by the 40 members of the Atlantic Coast Sports Media Association. In 16 games, he only allowed ten sacks and 58 total quarterback pressures. ===2013=== Castonzo returned in 2013 and started 16 consecutive games to help the Colts finish first in the [[AFC South]] with an 11–5 record. Pro Football Focus graded him +3.9 overall, −8.7 in pass blocking, and +11.2 in run blocking. Castonzo allowed only four sacks and was responsible for 62 quarterback pressures. His pass blocking grade ranked 56th among all offensive tackles in 2013. ===2014=== On April 28, 2014, the Indianapolis Colts opted to exercise the fifth-year, $7.438 million option on Castonzo's rookie contract.{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=April 28, 2014 |title=Colts exercise Castonzo's option |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/10852797/anthony-castonzo-indianapolis-colts-5th-year-option-exercised |access-date=August 8, 2015 |website=ESPN.com}} In Week 11, Castonzo recorded his first career reception and touchdown, catching a one-yard pass from [[Andrew Luck]]. He started all 16 games and played 1,115 snaps during the 2014 season, the most of any offensive lineman in the NFL.{{Cite web |last=Bowen |first=Kevin |date=February 11, 2015 |title=Anthony Castonzo Plays The Most Snaps Of Any NFL Offensive Lineman |url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Anthony-Castonzo-Plays-The-Most-Snaps-Of-Any-NFL-Offensive-Lineman/28104f8b-eab2-4603-a507-9ca2fde6fad4 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211202102/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Anthony-Castonzo-Plays-The-Most-Snaps-Of-Any-NFL-Offensive-Lineman/28104f8b-eab2-4603-a507-9ca2fde6fad4 |archive-date=February 11, 2015 |access-date=February 11, 2015 |website=colts.com}} [[Pro Football Focus]] gave him a grade of +18.5 overall. His pass blocking immensely improved as he received a grade +18.1 in pass blocking and −2.1 in run blocking. Castonzo ranked sixth among all qualifying offensive tackles in pass blocking grade and an overall grade ranked 12th out of 86 qualifying offensive tackles. Castonzo allowed only two sacks and 36 quarterback pressures as the [[2014 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] finish first in their division with an 11–5 record. PFF also ranked him the 66th best player on their 101 NFL Players of 2014 list. ===2015=== On September 10, 2015, the Indianapolis Colts signed Castonzo to a four-year, $43.81 million contract that includes $18 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $14 million. Castonzo started ten games at left tackle before suffering a knee sprain and missing three games (Weeks 12–14).{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2015 |title=Anthony Castonzo out with knee sprain |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2015/11/23/indianapolis-colts-anthony-castonzo-left-tackle-knee-injury/76278528/ |access-date=January 13, 2018 |website=Indystar.com}} He finished with 13 starts as the Indianapolis Colts finished second in the AFC South with an 8–8 record. Castonzo received the 12th highest grade among 84 qualifying offensive tackles from [[Pro Football Focus]] in 2015.{{Cite web |title=Rotoworld.com: Anthony Castonzo |url=http://www.rotoworld.com/recent/nfl/6519/anthony-castonzo |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=Rotoworld.com}} The entire Indianapolis Colts' offensive line was ranked 16th by PFF.{{Cite web |title=PFF Ranks Colts as Having NFL's 16th Best Offensive Line |url=https://horseshoeheroes.com/2016/07/12/pff-ranks-colts-as-having-nfls-16th-best-offensive-line/ |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=horseshowheroes.com}} ===2016=== Castonzo started all 16 games as the Indianapolis Colts finished third in the AFC South with an 8–8 record. ===2017=== Castonzo once again started all 16 games with the Colts, finishing third in the AFC South with a 4–12 record. ===2018=== After missing the first five games due to a hamstring injury, he made his season debut in Week 8, starting the final 11 games at left tackle.{{Cite web |title=Anthony Castonzo 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CastAn00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ===2020=== On March 15, 2020, Castonzo signed a two-year, $33 million contract extension with the Colts.{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=March 15, 2020 |title=Colts agree to contract extension with longtime LT Anthony Castonzo |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28907673/colts-agree-contract-extension-long-lt-anthony-castonzo |access-date=March 15, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}} On December 30, 2020, Castonzo had ankle surgery,{{Cite web |last=Dajani |first=Jordan |date=December 30, 2020 |title=Colts lose Anthony Castonzo for season as left tackle set for surgery on injured ankle |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/colts-lose-anthony-castonzo-for-season-as-left-tackle-set-for-surgery-on-injured-ankle/ |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=CBS Sports}}{{Cite web |last=A. Erickson |first=Joel |date=December 30, 2020 |title=Colts LT Anthony Castonzo out for the rest of the season |url=https://eu.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2020/12/30/colts-news-left-tackle-anthony-castonzo-out-rest-season/4088436001/ |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=IndyStar}} and he was placed on [[injured reserve]] two days later.{{Cite news |date=January 1, 2021 |title=Colts Place T Anthony Castonzo On Injured Reserve; Sign C Joey Hunt To Active Roster |work=Colts.com |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-place-t-anthony-castonzo-on-injured-reserve-sign-c-joey-hunt-to-active-ros |access-date=February 11, 2021}} On January 12, 2021, Castonzo announced his retirement from the NFL.{{Cite web |date=January 12, 2021 |title=Anthony Castonzo Announces His Retirement From NFL |url=https://www.colts.com/news/retirement-anthony-castonzo-jim-irsay-frank-reich-chris-ballard-2020-season |url-status=live |access-date=January 12, 2021 |website=Indianapolis Official Website|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112160212/https://www.colts.com/news/retirement-anthony-castonzo-jim-irsay-frank-reich-chris-ballard-2020-season |archive-date=January 12, 2021 }} ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== *[https://web.archive.org/web/20090807101507/http://bceagles.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/castonzo_anthony01.html Boston College Eagles bio] *{{commons category-inline}} {{2011 NFL Draft}} {{Indianapolis Colts 2011 draft navbox}} {{ColtsFirstPick}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Castonzo, Anthony}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Hawthorn Woods, Illinois]] [[Category:Players of American football from Lake County, Illinois]] [[Category:Players of American football from Park Ridge, Illinois]] [[Category:American football offensive tackles]] [[Category:Fork Union Military Academy alumni]] [[Category:Boston College Eagles football players]] [[Category:Indianapolis Colts players]]

'''Angelo King''' (born February 10, 1958) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Detroit Lions]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina State Bulldogs football|South Carolina State Bulldogs]].

==Early life==
King attended [[Columbia High School (Columbia, South Carolina)|Columbia High School]]. He accepted a football scholarship from the [[South Carolina State University]].

He was named a starter at [[linebacker]] midway through his freshman season, and was a part of the 1977 team that was awarded the National Black Championship by the [[Pittsburgh Courier]] newspaper.

King was a four-year starter that received [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference|All-MEAC]] honors in 1979 and 1980. He also received honorable-mention Little [[All-American]] honors in 1980.<ref>{{cite web | title=S.C. State to induct nine members, two teams into Athletic Hall of Fame tonight | website=The Times and Democrat | date=September 7, 2012 | url=https://thetandd.com/sports/bulldogzone/dish/s-c-state-to-induct-nine-members-two-teams-into/article_8793c430-f8af-11e1-a79a-0019bb2963f4.html | access-date=2025-10-24}}</ref> As a senior, he blocked a school record 4 punts (6 in his career).

In 2007, he was named to the [[South Carolina State University|South Carolina State]] Centennial Football Team. In 2012, he was inducted into the [[South Carolina State University|South Carolina State]] Athletic Hall of Fame.

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
King was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[1981 NFL draft]]. He was waived on August 3.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1979&dat=19810804&id=WxwyAAAAIBAJ&sjid=yKoFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5058,4663442 | title=Cowboys Release Seven; Cut Date Growing Nearer | access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref> He was re-signed and released again on August 25.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/422188417/ | title=Transactions | date=26 August 1981 | access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref> On September 8, he was re-signed after [[linebacker]] [[Mike Hegman]] fractured his arm in the season opener against the [[Washington Redskins]]. He played mainly on [[special teams]] and remained on the roster after Hegman returned.

He was mainly a nickel [[linebacker]] and [[special teams]] player for three seasons. On August 27, [[1984 NFL season|1984]], he was traded to the [[Detroit Lions]] in exchange for a sixth round draft choice (#151-[[Stan Gelbaugh]]).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1345&dat=19840828&id=VldOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=kfkDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5939,2613405 | title=Transactions | access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
King was a part-time starter and [[special teams]] player for the [[Detroit Lions]] in his first season with the team. In [[1985 NFL season|1985]], the team changed to a [[3-4 defense]] and although he was assigned the role of nickel linebacker, he eventually started 9 games after [[Mike Cofer (linebacker)|Michael Cofer]] was lost for the year and posted career-highs with 90 tackles (77 solo) and 4 sacks.

The next year, he missed 5 games with an ankle injury (4 weeks spent on the [[injured reserve list]]). After [[Jimmy Williams (linebacker)|Jimmy Williams]] was lost for the year, he started the last 4 games at [[strongside linebacker]] and finished with 23 tackles.

He was cut on September 6, [[1987 NFL season|1987]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1876&dat=19870908&id=4bQeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=vc4EAAAAIBAJ&pg=1813,2915140 | title=Transactions | access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref> After the players went on a strike on the third week of the season, those games were canceled (reducing the 16 game season to 15) and the [[NFL]] decided that the games would be played with replacement players. King was re-signed to be a part of the Lions replacement team, but was injured in the first game and placed on the [[injured reserve list]],<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1917&dat=19871005&id=qwshAAAAIBAJ&sjid=fXIFAAAAIBAJ&pg=3148,1205051 | title=Tripoli Excels As Bucs Tops Lions, 31-27 | access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref> before being released on October 27.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=110&dat=19871028&id=e8NRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0lUDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5631,4249876 | title=Lions release leading scorer | access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref>

'''Anthony Allen''' (born August 6, 1988) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]]  player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the seventh round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. His began his [[college football]] career with the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]] and set freshman rushing records. He then played the rest of his college career with the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]].

==Early life==
Allen attended [[Jesuit High School (Tampa)|Jesuit High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]].

==Professional career==

===Baltimore Ravens===
Allen was selected in the seventh round of the 2011 NFL draft by the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |access-date=2019-02-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2011 as the team's third running back, Allen received three carries for eight yards against the [[St. Louis Rams]]. He won his first Super Bowl ring after the Ravens defeated the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in [[Super Bowl XLVII]], 34–31. He was released by the team on August 30, 2013.

===Buffalo Bills===
On January 14, 2014, Allen signed a 2-year, $1.23M deal.  On May 12, 2014, the [[Buffalo Bills]] released Allen.<ref>{{cite web  | title=Bills release running back Anthony Allen | website=NBC Sports | date=2014-05-12 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bills-release-running-back-anthony-allen | access-date=2025-05-18}}</ref>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders (first stint)===
On June 7, 2014, Allen joined the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] at their training camp. During the off-season the Riders lost Grey Cup MVP [[Kory Sheets]] to the [[Oakland Raiders]]; leaving a vacancy at the running back position. Allen filled said position on the opening week of the season galloping to 158 rushing yards on 27 carries, with 1 rushing touchdown. Allen went on to be the main rushing back for the Riders in 2014, carrying the ball almost twice as much as any other player. By the close of the regular season he had 169 rushing attempts for 930 yards (5.5 average), with 5 touchdowns: Good enough for 2nd most rushing yards in the league, trailing only [[Jon Cornish]] who finished the campaign with 1,082 yards. He also made contributions in the passing game as well, amassing 244 yards on 36 receptions with 3 touchdowns.

===BC Lions===
Allen played in seven games for the [[BC Lions]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-allenant002 | title=Anthony Allen | publisher=statscrew.com | accessdate=May 25, 2024}}</ref>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders (second stint)===
Allen signed with the Roighriders on June 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2017/06/02/anthony-allen-returns-riderville/ | title=ANTHONY ALLEN RETURNS TO RIDERVILLE | publisher=cfl.ca | date=June 2, 2017 | accessdate=May 25, 2024}}</ref> He was released on June 17, 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tsn.ca/allen-tweets-frustration-with-roughriders-1.781999 | title=Allen tweets frustration with Roughriders | publisher=tsn.ca | date=June 17, 2017 | accessdate=May 25, 2024}}</ref>

'''Anthony Barr''' (born March 18, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]] from 2010 to 2013, earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2013. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the first round, ninth overall of the [[2014 NFL draft]].

Barr was an offensive player his first two years at UCLA, playing [[running back]], [[wide receiver]], and [[tight end]]. He struggled as a running back, and switched to linebacker during his junior year, at which position he was named a first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12]] selection and to the [[CBSSports.com]] All-America second-team. As a senior Barr received the [[Lott Trophy|Lott IMPACT Award]] after leading the team in [[Quarterback sack|sacks]].

In 2014, Barr's first season playing professional football in the NFL, he was named [[National Football Conference]] (NFC) Defensive Player of the Week for Week 8 and selected for the [[Pro Football Focus]] All-NFC North Team. His rookie season was cut short due to a knee injury. Following that season he made four consecutive [[Pro Bowl]] appearances (2015{{ndash}}2018). In the spring of 2019, he signed a five-year extension of his contract with the Vikings.

==Early life==
Barr was born in [[South Bend, Indiana]], but raised in [[Los Angeles]], where he attended [[Loyola High School (Los Angeles)|Loyola High School]] in the [[Pico-Union, Los Angeles|Pico-Union]] neighborhood. He was a [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] in football and track, and was an All-State selection at [[running back]] for the Loyola Cubs [[high school football|football]] team after rushing for 1,890 yards and 20 [[touchdowns]] as a junior.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wang |first1=Jack |url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20121225/ucla-junior-anthony-barr-enjoying-success-after-making-switch-this-season-to-linebacker-and-quickly-turns-into-a-hot-nfl-prospect |title=UCLA junior Anthony Barr enjoying success after making switch this season to linebacker – and quickly turns into a hot NFL prospect |newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News |date=December 24, 2012 |access-date=September 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222707/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20121225/ucla-junior-anthony-barr-enjoying-success-after-making-switch-this-season-to-linebacker-and-quickly-turns-into-a-hot-nfl-prospect |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, he missed virtually all of his senior season after breaking his ankle in the September, and was also unable to participate in the 2010 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]], to which he was invited.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Barr Biography – UCLA Bruins Official Athletic Site |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207914091 |website=uclabruins.com |access-date=December 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530024849/http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207914091&DB_OEM_ID=30500 |archive-date=May 30, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Barr also lettered four seasons in [[track and field]]. At the 2009 CIF Southern Prelims, he earned 11th-place finishes in both the [[100 metres|100 meter]] (11.01 s) and the [[200 metres|200 meter]] (22.40 s) dashes.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ca.milesplit.com/meets/54279/results/92626 |title=CIF Southern Section Division 2 Prelims. Regarded as a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Barr was listed as the No. 8 prospect and the No. 5 athlete out of the state of [[California]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals.com California PostseasonTop 100 |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=December 2, 2015 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-2489 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140516004420/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-2489 |archive-date=May 16, 2014}}</ref> According to [[Scout.com]], he was ranked as the No. 100 national prospect and the No. 10 outside linebacker. With scholarship offers from dozens of schools, Barr narrowed his decision down to [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] and UCLA, before choosing the Bruins on January 21, 2010.<ref>{{cite news |author=Nestor |title=Neuheisel Picks Up A Huge Recruit: 4 Star LB/RB Anthony Barr Picks UCLA Over Notre Dame |url=https://www.bruinsnation.com/2010/1/21/1264268/neuheisel-picks-up-a-huge-recruit |newspaper=Bruin Nation |date=January 21, 2010 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200101043303/https://www.bruinsnation.com/2010/1/21/1264268/neuheisel-picks-up-a-huge-recruit |archive-date=January 1, 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Barr was listed as one of the top linebacker prospects for the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Draft Scout |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/profilexnews.php?pyid=105122&draftyear=2014&genpos=OLB |website=NFL Draft Scout |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029185554/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/profilexnews.php?pyid=105122&draftyear=2014&genpos=OLB |archive-date=October 29, 2013 | year=2014}}</ref><ref name="SI.com mock 3.0" /> After the college season concluded, he was projected as the No. 3 selection in the 2014 NFL draft by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref name="SI.com mock 3.0">{{cite news |last1=Burke |first1=Chris |url=http://nfl.si.com/2013/12/03/2014-nfl-mock-draft-teddy-bridgewater-anthony-barr/ |title=2014 NFL Mock Draft 3.0 |newspaper=Sports Illustrated |date=December 3, 2013 |access-date=December 14, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131214102316/http://nfl.si.com/2013/12/03/2014-nfl-mock-draft-teddy-bridgewater-anthony-barr/ |archive-date=December 14, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> At the [[NFL Combine|2014 NFL Combine]], Barr ran the 40-yard dash in 4.66 seconds, sixth-best among linebackers, and tied for 14th in the vertical (34.5 inches). His 15 reps on the bench press were also dead last among those who participated, according to [[NFL.com]]'s combine tracker. At the UCLA [[Pro Day]] on March 11, he ran an electronic 4.41 in the [[40-yard dash]], did 19 repetitions on the [[bench press]] and had a 10-foot-5 (3.20 meters) [[broad jump]].

Barr was selected in the first round, ninth overall by the [[Minnesota Vikings]],<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Klein |first1=Gary |title=UCLA's Anthony Barr goes No. 9 overall to Minnesota Vikings |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/nfl/la-sp-nfl-draft-usc-ucla-20140509-story.html |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=May 8, 2014 |access-date=January 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328200151/http://www.latimes.com/sports/nfl/la-sp-nfl-draft-usc-ucla-20140509-story.html |archive-date=March 28, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> making him the highest selected defensive player out of UCLA since [[Eric Turner (American football)|Eric Turner]], second overall in [[1991 NFL draft|1991]]. He is the first UCLA player to be a top-10 selection since [[Jonathan Ogden]], who was selected fourth overall in [[1996 NFL draft|1996]]. He also surpassed [[Jamir Miller]], who was chosen tenth overall in [[1994 NFL draft|1994]], as the highest Bruins linebacker ever selected.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Breech |first1=John |title=2014 NFL Draft: Vikings get B for selecting LB Anthony Barr at No. 9 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/2014-nfl-draft-vikings-get-b-for-selecting-lb-anthony-barr-at-no-9/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=May 8, 2014 |access-date=December 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231220208/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/2014-nfl-draft-vikings-get-b-for-selecting-lb-anthony-barr-at-no-9/ |archive-date=December 31, 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Nate Cohn]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' in 2022 listed Barr and [[Ryan Mathews (American football)|Ryan Mathews]] as the only two of 19 top [[NFL draft]] picks since 2005 whose careers justified being chosen much earlier than their ESPN draft ranking.<ref name="cohn20220428">{{Cite news |last=Cohn |first=Nate |date=2022-04-28 |title=When Draft Pundits Are Right, and N.F.L. ===Minnesota Vikings (first stint)===
====2014 season====
[[File:Anthony Barr 2014 MV TC.jpg|right|thumb|Barr during 2014 training camp]]
Barr signed a four-year, $12.7 million contract with the Vikings. He received a $7.6 million signing bonus and the team could exercise a fifth-year option.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.twincities.com/vikings/ci_25799131/vikings-teddy-bridgewater-anthony-barr-sign-rookie-deals |title=Vikings' Teddy Bridgewater, Anthony Barr sign rookie deals |author=Chris Tomasson |date=May 20, 2014 |newspaper=St. Paul Pioneer Press |access-date=August 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006113102/http://www.twincities.com/vikings/ci_25799131/vikings-teddy-bridgewater-anthony-barr-sign-rookie-deals |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> Barr played in and started 12 games for the Vikings and was awarded [[National Football Conference]] (NFC) defensive player of the week for week 8.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Carlson|first1=Adam|title=Anthony Barr Named Defensive Player Of The Week For Week 8|url=https://thevikingage.com/2014/10/29/anthony-barr-named-defensive-player-week-week-8/|website=The Viking Age|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=December 31, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231062121/https://thevikingage.com/2014/10/29/anthony-barr-named-defensive-player-week-week-8/|archive-date=December 31, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Barr's 2014 season was cut short due to an injury and he was put on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carlson |first1=Adam |url=http://thevikingage.com/2014/12/27/anthony-barr-placed-minnesota-vikings-injured-reserve/ |title=Anthony Barr Placed On Minnesota Vikings Injured Reserve |date=December 27, 2014 |website=The Viking Age |access-date=March 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402142827/http://thevikingage.com/2014/12/27/anthony-barr-placed-minnesota-vikings-injured-reserve/ |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> He ended his rookie season with 70 combined tackles, four sacks, two forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries (one returned for a touchdown) and three pass deflections. He was a top contender for defensive rookie of the year and one of three Viking defenders named to the [[Pro Football Focus]] All-NFC North Team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mountford |first1=Michael |title=2014 All-NFC North Team |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/blog/2015/01/21/2014-pff-all-nfc-north-team/ |website=Pro Football Focus |access-date=January 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220132717/https://www.profootballfocus.com/blog/2015/01/21/2014-pff-all-nfc-north-team/ |archive-date=February 20, 2016 |date=January 21, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2015 season====
In the first game of the season, Barr played all 73 defensive snaps against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and recorded a career-high 12 tackles. He was credited with nine solo stops.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goessling |first1=Ben |title=Anthony Barr one of Vikings' few bright spots in loss to 49ers |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/minnesota-vikings/post/_/id/15302/anthony-barr-one-of-vikings-few-bright-spots-in-loss-to-49ers |website=ESPN.com |date=September 15, 2015 |access-date=December 31, 2019 31, 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> In a Week 4 loss against the eventual [[Super Bowl 50]] champions [[2015 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]], Barr recorded his first career [[interception]] off a pass thrown by [[Peyton Manning]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Anthony Barr, Harrison Smith pick off Peyton Manning |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/anthony-barr-harrison-smith-pick-off-peyton-manning-16009182 |website=vikings.com |date=October 4, 2015 |access-date=December 31, 2019 }}</ref> Barr broke his left hand in Week 9 (November 8), but in Week 12 he had a career-high eight tackles (seven solo), one sack, and forced two fumbles.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carlson |first1=Adam |url-status=live }}</ref> For the season, he totaled 68 tackles, four tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, eight quarterback hurries, one interception, seven passes defensed, and three forced fumbles. ====2016 season====
Barr struggled during the 2016 season, as he had only 37 solo tackles and two sacks.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ekstrom |first1=Sam |title=Anthony Barr Struggling to Make an Impact in His Third Season |url=https://zonecoverage.com/2016/minnesota-vikings-news/anthony-barr-struggling-to-make-an-impact-in-his-third-season/ |website=zonecoverage.com |access-date=December 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231204011/https://zonecoverage.com/2016/minnesota-vikings-news/anthony-barr-struggling-to-make-an-impact-in-his-third-season/ |archive-date=December 31, 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> Despite a poor season in which coach Zimmer stated that Barr had a "tendency to coast,"<ref>{{cite news|title=Vikings' Mike Zimmer: Anthony Barr has 'tendency to coast'|url=http://www.twincities.com/2016/12/21/vikings-mike-zimmer-anthony-barr-has-tendency-to-coast/|author=Tomasson, Chris|newspaper=St. Paul Pioneer Press|date=December 22, 2016|access-date=January 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202082316/http://www.twincities.com/2016/12/21/vikings-mike-zimmer-anthony-barr-has-tendency-to-coast/|archive-date=February 2, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Barr was named to his second straight Pro Bowl.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vensel |first1=Matt |title=Despite disappointing 2016 season, Anthony Barr earns Pro Bowl invite |url=http://www.startribune.com/despite-a-disappointing-season-anthony-barr-earns-pro-bowl-invite/411526225/ |newspaper=Star Tribune |date=January 23, 2017 |access-date=January 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107015251/http://www.startribune.com/despite-a-disappointing-season-anthony-barr-earns-pro-bowl-invite/411526225/ |archive-date=January 7, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2017 season====
On May 1, 2017, the Vikings exercised the fifth year option on Barr's contract. Barr had 75 tackles, 33 solo tackles, 52 assisted tackles, and one sack. On December 19, 2017, Barr was named to his third straight Pro Bowl.<ref>{{cite web|title=NFL announces 2018 Pro Bowl rosters|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/updated-player-rosters-for-2018-pro-bowl-in-orlando-0ap3000000895772|website=NFL.com|date=December 19, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171220125215/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000895772/article/nfl-announces-2018-pro-bowl-rosters|archive-date=December 20, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the [[2019–20 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 49ers 27, Minnesota Vikings 10|divisional round]] of the playoffs against the 49ers, Barr forced a fumble on running back [[Matt Breida]] and recovered the football, but the Vikings lost 27–10.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131040 |title=49ers win 1st playoff game in 6 years, 27-10 over Vikings |date=January 11, 2020|agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref>

====2020 season====
Barr was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Vikings on July 30, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Minnesota Vikings Player Updates On Reserve/COVID-19 List |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/covid-19-players-reserve-opt-out-nfl-2020 |website=Vikings.com |date=July 30, 2020 |access-date=July 30, 2020}}</ref> and activated from the list four days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves to Set Roster at 80 Players |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/pj-hall-anthony-barr-ifeadi-odenigbo-quartney-davis-roster-moves |website=Vikings.com |date=August 3, 2020 |access-date=August 3, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 21, 2020, after suffering a torn [[pectoral muscle]] in Week 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings place Anthony Barr on injured reserve|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/21/vikings-place-anthony-barr-on-injured-reserve/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sport|date=September 21, 2020}}</ref> He missed the last 14 games of the season.

====2021 season====
In March, the team reworked his contract and Barr was allowed to become a free agent at the end of the season. In August, he underwent a surgery procedure for an injury he suffered in his right knee during [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]]. He missed the first four games of the season, while recovering from the knee injury.

In the ninth game against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], he was declared inactive. In the eleventh game against the 49ers, he suffered a right hamstring injury. He missed the following game against the [[Detroit Lions]]. He finished with 11 starts, 72 tackles, 3 interceptions (career-high), 2.5 sacks, and 3 tackles for loss.

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 3, 2022, Barr signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |last2=Cronin |first2=Courtney |date=2022-08-03 |title=Cowboys, veteran LB Barr reach 1-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34342825/anthony-barr-dallas-cowboys-agree-one-year-deal |access-date=2024-10-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He was acquired to provide depth at the linebacking corps. In the eighth game against the [[Chicago Bears]], he suffered a hamstring strain injury late in the second quarter, which also forced him to miss the following three games against the Packers, Vikings and Giants. He appeared in 14 games with 10 starts, collecting 61 tackles, 2 fumble recoveries and one pass defensed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Barr 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BarrAn00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2025-05-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He wasn't re-signed after the season.

===Minnesota Vikings (second stint)===
On November 14, 2023, Barr re-signed with the Vikings to their [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Peters | first=Craig | title=Vikings Sign Anthony Barr to Practice Squad | website=Vikings.com | date=2023-11-14 | url=https://www.vikings.com/news/anthony-barr-linebacker-sign-practice-squad | access-date=2025-05-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet|user=Vikings|number=1724493473443721361|date=November 14, 2023|title=The #Vikings have officially signed LB Anthony Barr to the practice squad}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on December 29.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Lindsey |date=December 29, 2023 |title=Vikings Sign Anthony Barr to Active Roster; Nick Vigil to Practice Squad |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/sign-anthony-barr-active-roster-nick-vigil-practice-squad |access-date=29 December 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> 

After not playing in 2024, Barr announced his retirement from professional football on August 4, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Florio |first1=Mike |title=Anthony Barr, a top-10 pick in 2014, retires |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/anthony-barr-a-top-10-pick-in-2014-retires |website=NBC Sports |access-date=6 August 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Barr's father, [[Tony Brooks (American football)|Tony Brooks]], and uncles, [[Reggie Brooks]] and [[Cedric Figaro]], all played in the [[National Football League|NFL]]. All of them also played at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]].<ref>{{cite news | last1=Foster | first1=Chris | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2010-sep-02-la-sp-anthony-barr-ucla-20100903-story.html | title=It's Westwood, not South Bend, for Anthony Barr, UCLA's new 'F-back' | newspaper=Los Angeles Times | date=September 2, 2010 | access-date=December 4, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221131415/http://articles.latimes.com/2010/sep/02/sports/la-sp-anthony-barr-ucla-20100903 | archive-date=February 21, 2014 | url-status=live }}</ref> Shortly after his birth in South Bend, Barr and his mother moved to the suburbs of Los Angeles where he was raised by his mother and maternal grandparents.<ref name=CTomasson/>

In 2016, Anthony Barr established "Raise the Barr", a nonprofit initiative to assist single-parent undergraduate students in [[Minnesota]] and [[California]] complete their post-secondary education by providing comprehensive resources to both parents and children. It raised over $250,000 to single parents and provided them with college and emergency grants.<ref name=CTomasson/> On June 27, 2018, it launched new emergency grant funding at Loyola High School, raising $50,000 in assistance, ticket sales, and auctioning.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Lindsey |title=Anthony Barr Launches Raise the Barr Emergency Grant Fund for Single Parents |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/anthony-barr-s-foundation-unveils-new-emergency-grant-fund |website=vikings.com |access-date=January 4, 2020 |date=July 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726111322/https://www.vikings.com/news/anthony-barr-s-foundation-unveils-new-emergency-grant-fund |archive-date=July 26, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Andy Leon Mulumba Kabaluapa''' (born January 31, 1990) is a [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]]-[[Canada|Canadian]] former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for [[Eastern Michigan University|Eastern Michigan]].<ref>[http://www.emueagles.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3355 Eastern Michigan bio]</ref> He was selected by the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] second overall<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bluebombers.com/article/blue-bombers-select-andy-mulumba-with-second-overall-pick |title=BLUE BOMBERS SELECT ANDY MULUMBA WITH SECOND OVERALL PICK |access-date=May 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026014159/http://www.bluebombers.com/article/blue-bombers-select-andy-mulumba-with-second-overall-pick |archive-date=October 26, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> in the [[2013 CFL draft]] but subsequently signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].

==Early life==
Mulumba was born one of six children to parents Martin Kabaluapa and Madeleine Bipendu. He has three brothers and two sisters. Mulumba played football in [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]] during which he played as a [[Lineman (gridiron football)|defensive lineman]]. For his role in the national championship victory, Mulumba was named the team's Defensive Most Valuable Player.<ref name="EMU's Andy Mulumba">[https://emueagles.com/sports/football/roster/andy-mulumba/3975 "Andy Mulumba"]'s EMU Eagles Profile. Retrieved August 26, 2024.</ref>  

==College career==
Mulumba joined the [[Eastern Michigan University]] football team, entering the 2009 season as a true freshman. He played in all 12 games after which Mulumba was one of nine players to earn a letter. Mulumba began as a linebacker before transitioning into the defensive line position by his sophomore season. While as a junior during the 2011 season, Mulumba was named to the Academic All-MAC Team. He also earned two letters during his first two seasons.<ref name="EMU's Andy Mulumba"/>

==Professional career==

===Green Bay Packers===
After going undrafted  in the [[2013 NFL draft]], Mulumba signed with the Green Bay Packers as an [[undrafted free agent]] May 10, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-1/Packers-sign-nine-draft-choices-nine-undrafted-free-agents/f4309bf1-b665-4867-9469-57622511f123 |title=Packers sign nine draft choices, nine undrafted free agents |access-date=December 14, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160110201944/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-1/Packers-sign-nine-draft-choices-nine-undrafted-free-agents/f4309bf1-b665-4867-9469-57622511f123 |archive-date=January 10, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On September 17, Mulumba was diagnosed with a torn ACL.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Packers lose linebacker Mulumba to ACL|url = https://www.espn.com/blog/green-bay-packers/post/_/id/13227/packers-lose-linebacker-mulumba-to-acl|website = ESPN.com| date=September 17, 2014 |access-date = December 4, 2015}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On April 1, 2016, Mulumba signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. On September 3, 2016, he was released by the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Down to NFL Mandated Roster Limit|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Down-to-NFL-Mandated-Roster-Limit/eaa26747-962f-4a0c-a143-502c64f318ed|website=Chiefs.com|access-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013185227/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Down-to-NFL-Mandated-Roster-Limit/eaa26747-962f-4a0c-a143-502c64f318ed|archive-date=October 13, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
On January 2, 2017, Mulumba signed a futures contract with the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign Two Reserve/Future Free Agents|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-Two-ReserveFuture-Free-Agents/97b65ebc-a464-485e-9d0f-9bfd8078952e|website=Raiders.com|date=January 2, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on July 7, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/55397347-d8df-49c3-8abc-b55dc19919fa?sf96293637=1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105070712/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/55397347-d8df-49c3-8abc-b55dc19919fa?sf96293637=1|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 5, 2018|website=Raiders.com|date=July 7, 2017}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On July 27, 2017, Mulumba signed with the [[Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Sign Four Players|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Sign-Four-Players-/ef47b22b-0737-4855-ae71-19e672780034|author=Lago, Kristen|website=TheRams.com|date=July 27, 2017|access-date=July 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729005516/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Sign-Four-Players-/ef47b22b-0737-4855-ae71-19e672780034|archive-date=July 29, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Announce Roster Moves|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Announce-Roster-Moves/33a04e1d-a581-47b1-a2ef-75984001a240|author=Han, Jamie|website=TheRams.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208051619/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Announce-Roster-Moves/33a04e1d-a581-47b1-a2ef-75984001a240|archivedate=February 8, 2018}}</ref>

'''Angel Rubio''' (born April 12, 1975) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for one season with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the seventh round of the [[1998 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks football|Southeast Missouri State Redhawks]]. He was also a member of the [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Orlando Predators]], [[Las Vegas Outlaws (XFL)|Las Vegas Outlaws]], [[Detroit Fury]], [[Dallas Desperados]], and [[Austin Wranglers]].

==Early life==
Rubio garnered All-District and All-League recognition at [[Ceres High School]] in [[Ceres, California]].<ref name="A"/>

==College career==
Rubio played for the [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks football|Southeast Missouri State Redhawks]] from 1993 to 1997, recording a total of 330 tackles.<ref name="L">{{cite web|url=http://gosoutheast.com/hof.aspx?hof=99&path=&kiosk= |title=Southeast Missouri Athletics Hall of Fame |publisher=gosoutheast.com |access-date=July 30, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown '''Howard Andrew Spiva''' (February 6, 1955 – April 3, 1979) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He appeared in 13 games for the Falcons in 1977. He was killed in a car accident. Teammate [[Garth TenNapel]] was in the same vehicle and was seriously injured.

==Biography==
Spiva was born on February 6, 1955, in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]]. He attended [[Chamblee High School]] in [[Chamblee, Georgia]] and the [[University of Tennessee]].<ref name=PFR/> At Tennessee, Spiva was a two-time All-Southeastern Conference selection.<ref name="Mourn">{{Cite news |date=April 4, 1979 |title=Falcons mourn death of linebacker Spiva |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1891&dat=19790404&id=jKUfAAAAIBAJ&sjid=RdYEAAAAIBAJ&pg=5622,878858 |access-date=September 6, 2014 |work=[[Gadsden Times]]|via=Google News}}</ref> He was drafted by the [[St. Louis Cardinals (football)|St. Louis Cardinals]] in the fifth round of the [[1977 NFL draft]] with the 135th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1977 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1977/draft.htm |access-date=March 2, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Spiva was released by St. Louis that year when the team made its final preseason cuts.<ref name=SG>{{cite news|title=Andy Spiva dies after auto crash|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1917&dat=19790404&id=kgUxAAAAIBAJ&sjid=ieAFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1938,1013794|accessdate=September 6, 2014|work=[[Schenectady Gazette]]|via=Google News|date=April 4, 1979}}</ref> He was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] shortly thereafter.<ref name=GT>{{cite news|title=Wednesday transactions|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2202&dat=19770922&id=yo0yAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9OgFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1856,3114314|accessdate=September 6, 2014|via=Google News|work=[[The Gettysburg Times]]|date=September 22, 1977}}</ref> Falcons coach [[Leeman Bennett]] said that the team had become impressed with Spiva when they played Spiva and the Cardinals in a preseason game.<ref name="Signed">{{Cite news |date=September 22, 1977 |title=Spiva signed |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=348&dat=19770922&id=SNkvAAAAIBAJ&sjid=CDMDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5539,2997619 |access-date=September 6, 2014 |via=Google News|work=[[Rome News-Tribune]]}}</ref>

He played in 13 games for the Falcons in 1977.<ref name="PFR">{{Cite web |title=Andy Spiva Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SpivAn20.htm |access-date=March 2, 2024 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |language=en}}</ref> Prior to the 1978 season, Spiva was the top middle linebacker on Atlanta's depth chart before suffering a preseason knee injury.<ref name=OR>{{cite news|title=Spiva killed in accident|via=Google News|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2519&dat=19790404&id=O-5dAAAAIBAJ&sjid=eV8NAAAAIBAJ&pg=2912,463231|accessdate=September 6, 2014|work=[[Observer–Reporter]]|date=April 4, 1979}}</ref> He underwent surgery to repair torn ligaments a few days after sustaining the injury.<ref name=Long>{{cite news|title=Spiva has long, hard time ahead|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=348&dat=19780822&id=I-0uAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0jIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4229,3022678|via=Google News|accessdate=September 6, 2014|work=[[Rome News-Tribune]]|date=August 22, 1978}}</ref>

On April 3, 1979, Spiva was driving in rainy conditions when his sports car slid off of a street in the Atlanta area and it collided with a tree. Spiva died at Northside Hospital that day after sustaining head and chest injuries. His teammate [[Garth TenNapel]] was seriously injured in the crash.<ref name=Dies>{{cite news|title=Falcons' Andy Spiva dies|via=Google News|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1665&dat=19790402&id=trIjAAAAIBAJ&sjid=KiQEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1489,3676955|accessdate=September 6, 2014|work=[[Times-News (Hendersonville, North Carolina)]]|date=April 4, 1979}}</ref> Spiva and TenNapel had been close friends since going through knee rehabilitation together the previous year.<ref name=OR/>

'''Anthony Quantrell Brown'''<ref name="Pfa"/> (born November 6, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]].

==Early life and college==
Brown grew up as a [[military brat]].<ref name="Pit">{{cite web | url=https://steelerstakeaways.com/exclusive-with-former-steelers-offensive-lineman-anthony-brown-1999/ | title=Exclusive with Former Steelers Offensive Lineman Anthony Brown, 1999 | publisher=steelerstakeaways.com | date=November 30, 2022 | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He was born on November 6, 1972, in [[Okinawa, Japan]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/brow00750.html | title=Anthony Brown | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Würzburg American High School]] in [[Würzburg, Germany]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

He was a member of the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] from 1991 to 1992 and a two-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1993 to 1994.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was named a third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121598aaa.html |title=Associated Press |access-date=March 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223170809/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121598aaa.html |archive-date=February 23, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1995 NFL draft]], Brown signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on April 26.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in seven games, starting one, for the Bengals during his rookie year in 1995.<ref name="Pfr"/> He appeared in seven games in 1996 and six games in 1997. He became a free agent after the 1997 season and re-signed with the team on February 13, 1998.<ref name="Pfr"/><ref name="transactions"/> Brown played in all 16 games, starting five, for the Bengals in 1998.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAn20.htm | title=Anthony Brown | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He became a free agent again after the 1998 season.<ref name="transactions"/>

Brown was signed by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] on April 23, 1999.<ref name="transactions"/> He appeared in 16 games, starting 11, in 1999.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released by the Steelers on August 27, 2000.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/brow00750.html | title=Anthony Brown NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brown's older brother [[Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)|Mike Brown]] is the head coach of the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], and won a championship with the Knicks in [[2026 NBA Finals|2026.]]

He has spent time working in real estate after his NFL career.<ref name="Pit"/>

'''Anthony Shaquille Brown '''  (born December 15, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Purdue University|Purdue Boilermakers]] and was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in the sixth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Brown attended [[Hillsborough High School (Tampa, Florida)|Hillsborough High School]], where he played [[high school football|football]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Brown, Hillsborough, Athlete |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Anthony-Brown-14571/high-school-7166/ |access-date=October 19, 2020 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He was a two-year starter and received second-team All-Hillsborough County honors. As a junior, he tallied 69 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], one [[interception]], one [[pass defensed]] and four [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 52 yards. In his last year he was a [[two-way player]], posting 25 tackles, two interceptions, three passes defensed, 911 rushing yards, 14 rushing [[touchdowns]], 18 receptions for 239 yards and one touchdown. He also practiced [[track and field|track]].
