====2016====
The [[Dallas Cowboys]] selected Brown in the sixth round with the 189th overall pick in the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Brown was the 27th [[cornerback]] drafted in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 26, 2016 |title=Cowboys fill big need by drafting Purdue CB Anthony Brown in Round 6 |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-cowboys/cowboys/2016/04/30/cowboys-draft-purdue-cb-anthony-brown-round-6 |access-date=November 2, 2018 |newspaper=Dallas News}}</ref> On May 18, 2016, the Cowboys signed Brown to a four-year, $2.47 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $134,947.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Anthony Brown contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/dallas-cowboys/anthony-brown-19143/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Brown competed to be a backup cornerback against [[Josh Thomas (cornerback)|Josh Thomas]], [[Isaiah Frey]], [[Dax Swanson]], and [[Deji Olatoye]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 13, 2016 |title=Players to Watch at Minicamp: Rookie Cornerback Anthony Brown |url=http://www.5pointsblue.com/players-watch-minicamp-rookie-cornerback-anthony-brown/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109153126/http://www.5pointsblue.com/players-watch-minicamp-rookie-cornerback-anthony-brown/ |archive-date=November 9, 2018 |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=5pointsblue.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman, David |date=June 13, 2016 |title=Cowboys Fill Out Roster By Signing Two New Cornerbacks |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-fill-out-roster-by-signing-two-new-cornerbacks-405971 |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Jason Garrett]] named Brown the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to start the regular season. He began the season behind [[Brandon Carr]], [[Morris Claiborne]], and [[Orlando Scandrick]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2016 |title=Dallas Cowboys Release Depth Chart For Week 1 vs. New York Giants |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2016/9/9/12813750/2016-dallas-cowboys-official-depth-chart-for-week-1-vs-new-york-giants |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=BloggingtheBoys}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Cowboys’ season-opener against the [[New York Giants]] and made one solo tackle during their 20–19 loss. On September 25, 2016, Brown earned his first career start in place of Orlando Scandrick who was inactive due to a [[hamstring]] injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2016 |title=Report: Orlando Scandrick out with hamstring injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/report-orlando-scandrick-out-with-hamstring-injury/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=cbssports.com}}</ref> Brown finished the Cowboys’ 31–17 victory against the [[Chicago Bears]] with four combined tackles. In Week 6, he collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (ten solo) during a 30–16 win at the [[Green Bay Packers]]. Brown began to see extended play beginning in Week 9 of the season after [[Morris Claiborne]] sustained a groin injury the previous week.<ref>{{Cite web |title=After early pass, Cowboys land corner in sixth with Anthony Brown |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4750822/after-early-pass-cowboys-land-corner-in-6th-with-anthony-brown |access-date=April 30, 2016}}</ref> On December 11, 2016, Brown recorded two solo tackles, broke up a pass, and made his first career interception as the Cowboys lost 10–7 at the New York Giants in Week 14. Brown intercepted a pass attempt by Giants’ quarterback [[Eli Manning]], that was originally intended for wide receiver [[Victor Cruz (American football)|Victor Cruz]] in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants – December 11, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612110nyg.htm |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in 2016 with 55 combined tackles (40 solo), eight pass deflections, and one interception in 16 games and nine starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Anthony Brown (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/anthonybrown/2555531/careerstats |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Dallas Cowboys finished first in the [[NFC East]] with a 13–3 record and earned a first round bye. On January 15, 2017, Brown recorded one tackle during a 34–31 loss to the Packers in the NFC Divisional Round.

====2017====
Brown entered training camp as a possible candidate to win the role as a starting cornerback after Brandon Carr departed in free agency. He competed against Orlando Scandrick, [[Nolan Carroll]], [[Chidobe Awuzie]], and [[Jourdan Lewis]]. Head coach Jason Garrett named Brown the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind Orlando Scandrick, Nolan Carroll, and Chidobe Awuzie.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Predicting Cowboys 2017 initial depth chart after final roster cuts |url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2017/09/02/dallas-cowboys-2017-depth-chart-53-man-roster-projection-final-cuts/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=cowboyswire.usatoday.com}}</ref>

He appeared in the Cowboys’ season-opener against the Giants on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'' and recorded one solo tackle, broke up a pass, and intercepted a pass by Giants’ quarterback [[Eli Manning]] in the fourth quarter of their 19–3 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Dallas Cowboys – September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100dal.htm |access-date=October 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> The following week, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles during a 42–17 loss at the [[Denver Broncos]] in Week 2. He earned his first start of the season in Week 2 after Nolan Carroll suffered a concussion and was subsequently released on October 11, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davison, Drew |date=September 18, 2017 |title=What's next for ailing Dallas Cowboys? |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nfl/dallas-cowboys/article174041361.html |access-date=November 2, 2018 |newspaper=Star-Telegram}}</ref> Brown started the next ten games, but was eventually benched for Chidobe Awuzie in Week 13 and remained a backup for the last five games of the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2017 |title=Cowboys CB Anthony Brown suffering major sophomore slump |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/dallas-cowboys/article/anthony-browns-sophomore-slump-could-open-door-for-dallas-cowboys-rookie-cb-chidobe-awuzie-110781716/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> On December 31, 2017, Brown recorded six combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made his first career sack in the Cowboys’ 6–0 win at the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 17. Brown sacked Eagles’ backup quarterback [[Nate Sudfeld]] for a 14-yard loss in the third quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles – December 31st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712310phi.htm |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Brown finished the [[2017 NFL season]] with 56 combined tackles (47 solo), 11 pass deflections, two interceptions, and a sack in 16 games and ten starts.<ref name="career" />

====2018====
[[File:Anthony Brown (45433440412) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Brown in a game against the [[Washington Redskins]] ]]
During training camp, Brown competed to be a starting cornerback against [[Byron Jones (American football)|Byron Jones]] after Jones was moved from free safety to cornerback.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 8, 2018 |title=Anthony Brown hungry, embracing new competition from Byron Jones |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/dallas-cowboys/article/cowboys-cb-anthony-brown-hungry-embracing-added-competition-from-byron-jones-115966155/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> Head coach Jason Garrett named Brown the third cornerback and first-team nickelback on the Cowboys’ depth chart to begin the regular season. He was listed on the depth chart behind Chidobe Awuzie and Byron Jones.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2018 |title=Cowboys release depth chart for season opener vs. Panthers |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/dallas-cowboys/ContentGallery/Cowboys-depth-chart-vs-Panthers-121451664/ |access-date=November 2, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>

====2019====
Brown entered the 2019 season as the third cornerback on the depth chart behind Byron Jones and Chidobe Awuzie. In Week 11, Brown suffered a torn triceps and was ruled out the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=November 18, 2019 |title=Anthony Brown out for the year with a torn triceps |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/11/18/anthony-brown-out-for-the-year-with-a-torn-triceps/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> He finished the season playing in nine games with four starts, recording 17 tackles and five passes defensed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Brown 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAn02/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=October 19, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2020====
Brown re-signed with the Cowboys on a three-year contract on March 20, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Transactions March 2020 |url=http://www.nfl.com/transactions?transactionMonth=3&transactionYear=2020&transactionTeamAbbr= |access-date=March 22, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Archer, Todd |date=March 18, 2020 |title=Source: Anthony Brown returns to Cowboys on 3-year deal |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28922707/source-anthony-brown-returns-cowboys-3-year-deal |access-date=March 22, 2020}}</ref> On September 19, 2020, he was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a rib injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman, David |date=September 19, 2020 |title=Anthony Brown To IR; OT Signed From P. Squad |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/anthony-brown-to-ir-ot-signed-from-p-squad |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> He was designated to return from injured reserve on October 7, and began practicing with the team again.<ref>{{cite news |author=Phillips, Rob |title=Practice Report: Gregory Returns; LVE Closer? |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/practice-report-gregory-returns-lve-closer |website=DallasCowboys.com |date=October 7, 2020 |access-date=October 26, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on October 10.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2020 |title=Cowboys roster move: Anthony Brown returns, Francis Bernard promoted, Tyron Smith and Joe Looney to IR |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2020/10/10/21510824/cowboys-roster-move-anthony-brown-returns-francis-bernard-promoted-tyron-smith-and-joe-looney-to-ir |website=Blogging the Boys |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> In Week 5 against the Giants, Brown returned a fumble forced by teammate [[DeMarcus Lawrence]] on [[Daniel Jones (American football)|Daniel Jones]] for a 29-yard touchdown during the 37–34 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Dallas Cowboys – October 11th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110dal.htm |access-date=October 11, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 15 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Brown recorded his first interception of the season off a pass thrown by [[Nick Mullens]] during the 41–33 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys - December 20th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012200dal.htm |access-date=2020-12-20 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2021====
Brown was named the starter at right cornerback, helping fill the void left by [[Chidobe Awuzie]]'s departure in free agency. In a Week 12 36–33 Cowboys loss to the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] on [[NFL on Thanksgiving|Thanksgiving]], Brown committed 4 defensive [[pass interference]] penalties for 91 yards, including one to set up the Raiders' game-winning field goal in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cowboys-cb-anthony-brown-on-frustrating-four-dpi-penalties-it-s-just-one-of-them|title=Cowboys CB Anthony Brown on 'frustrating' four DPI penalties: 'It's just one of them days'|website=NFL.com|access-date=November 29, 2021}}</ref> He was the first player since at least 2000 to commit 4 pass interference penalties in a single game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dmagazine.com/sports/2021/11/the-cowboys-number-to-know-91-week-12-versus-las-vegas/|title=The Cowboys Number to Know: 91 (Week 12 versus Las Vegas)|website=DMagazine|access-date=November 29, 2021}}</ref> However, Brown statistically had the best season of his career, as he accumulated career-highs with 16 starts, 79 tackles (third on the team), 3 interceptions (tied for second on the team), 17 passes defensed (second on the team), one forced fumble and one defensive touchdown.

====2022====
Brown returned as the Cowboys starting cornerback in 2022. He suffered a torn [[Achilles tendon]] in Week 13 and was placed on season-ending injured reserve on December 10, 2022.

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On August 30, 2023, Brown was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers add nine to the practice squad|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-add-nine-to-the-practice-squad|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> He was released on September 14.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make multiple roster moves|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-multiple-roster-moves-x3687|website=Steelers.com|date=September 14, 2023}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On September 19, 2023, Brown signed a one-year contract with the 49ers, but was released on September 21.<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign CB Anthony Brown to a One-Year Deal|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-cornerback-anthony-brown-to-a-one-year-deal|website=49ers.com|date=September 19, 2023|access-date=September 20, 2023}}</ref> On September 22, the 49ers re-signed Brown to a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Re-Sign CB Brown; Waive CB Swilling|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-re-sign-cb-brown-waive-cb-swilling|website=49ers.com|date=September 22, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2023}}</ref> He was released by the 49ers on October 31.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-release-a-cornerback-and-announce-other-roster-moves|work=49ers.com|title=49ers Release a Cornerback and Announce Other Roster Moves|date=October 31, 2023|accessdate=October 31, 2023}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On November 28, 2023, Brown was signed to the [[New York Jets]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greenberg |first1=Ethan |title=Jets Sign CB Anthony Brown to Practice Squad |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-cb-anthony-brown-to-practice-squad-11-28-2023 |website=newyorkjets.com |access-date=29 November 2023}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season and thus became a free agent upon the expiration of his practice squad contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-nine-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-01-08-2024|website=newyorkjets.com|title=Jets Sign Nine Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |date=January 8, 2024|author=Greenberg, Ethan}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On August 3, 2024, Brown signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref name="g283">{{cite web | last=Hill | first=Kassidy | title=Panthers make second series of moves on Saturday, adding a corner | website=Panthers.com | date=2024-08-03 | url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-second-series-of-moves-on-saturday-adding-a-corner | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 19.<ref>{{cite web|title=Injuries force a handful of transactions Monday|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/injuries-force-a-handful-of-transactions-monday|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 19, 2024}}</ref> He was released on December 17.<ref name="q236">{{cite web | last=Rizzuti | first=Anthony | title=Panthers part ways with veteran CB on Tuesday | website=Panthers Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-12-17 | url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2024/12/17/panthers-waive-anthony-brown-ir-cowboys/ | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref>

'''Anthony Averett''' (born November 30, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]].

==Early life==
Averett attended [[Woodbury Junior-Senior High School]] in [[Woodbury, New Jersey]]. He played [[high school football|football]] and ran [[track and field|track]] in high school. At the 2012 [[Penn Relays]], he placed second in the [[long jump]]. His senior year, he was one of the best high school long jumpers in the nation,  with a jump of 25 feet, two inches, which was the second-longest jump in New Jersey history. He also ran 10.6 seconds in the 100-meters, 6.46 seconds in the 55 meters and high jumped 6 feet, 4 inches.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Averett - Football |url=https://rolltide.com/sports/football/roster/anthony-averett/3883 |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=University of Alabama Athletics |language=en}}</ref> In football, he played [[defensive back]] and [[quarterback]]. Averett committed to the [[University of Alabama]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2013 |title=Anthony Averett to Alabama: Woodbury native makes National Signing Day decision |url=http://blog.nj.com/southjerseyhssports/2013/02/woodburys_anthony_averett_sign.html |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=NJ.com|via=South Jersey Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Averett [[redshirted]] his first year at Alabama in 2013 and played in only one game in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anastasia |first=Phil |date=October 1, 2016 |title=Perseverance pays off for ex-Woodbury star Anthony Averett |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/high_school/new_jersey/20161002_Perseverance_pays_off_for_ex-Woodbury_star_Anthony_Averett.html |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=Inquirer.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2015, he played [[special teams]], recording two [[tackled gridiron|tackles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zenitz |first=Matt |date=June 15, 2016 |title=Speedy Tide DB continues to progress, optimistic heading into fall |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2016/06/speedy_alabama_cornerback_cont.html |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=AL.com |language=en}}</ref> Averett became a starter in 2016 and played in all 15 games, finishing with 48 tackles, one [[interception]] and also one [[qb sack|sack]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zenitz |first=Matt |date=March 27, 2017 |title=Alabama's Adoree' Jackson? Tide DB poised for big year |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2017/03/alabamas_adoree_jackson_tide_c.html |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=AL.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Suttles |first=Aaron |date=August 15, 2017 |title=Alabama DB Anthony Averett says he's more experienced, healthy this year |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/2017/08/15/alabama-db-anthony-averett-says-hes-more-experienced-healthy-this-year/19612450007/ |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=The Tuscaloosa News |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Averett was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fourth round, 118th overall, of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink, Ryan |date=April 28, 2018 |title=Round 4: Ravens Select CB Anthony Averett at No. 118 |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/round-4-ravens-select-cb-anthony-averett-at-no-118-20604029 |access-date=May 19, 2018 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

On October 22, 2020, Averett was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a shoulder injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=October 22, 2020 |title=Brandon Williams Off Reserve/COVID-19 List, Anthony Averett Goes on IR |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/brandon-williams-off-reserve-covid-19-list-anthony-averett-goes-on-ir |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He was activated on December 8, 2020.

On October 3, 2021, Averett intercepted [[Denver Broncos]] quarterback [[Drew Lock]] in the end zone, and helped the Ravens win 23–7.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=December 8, 2020 |title=Anthony Averett Activated, Two Called Up From Practice Squad |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/anthony-averett-activated-two-called-up-from-practice-squad |access-date=January 17, 2021 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> On December 26, in the team's Week 16 game against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Averett suffered a fractured rib after taking a hit from Bengals tight end [[C. J. Uzomah]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sobus |first=Robert |date=December 28, 2021 |title=Ravens HC John Harbaugh gives another injury update on CB Anthony Averett |url=https://ravenswire.usatoday.com/2021/12/27/ravens-hc-john-harbaugh-gives-another-injury-update-on-cb-anthony-averett/ |access-date=April 23, 2022 |website=Ravens Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
Averett signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] on March 17, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2022 |title=Raiders sign CB Anthony Averett |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-cb-anthony-averett-nfl-2022-free-agency-offseason |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417170822/https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-cb-anthony-averett-nfl-2022-free-agency-offseason |archive-date=April 17, 2022 |access-date=March 20, 2022 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 12, 2022, after suffering a broken thumb in Week 1.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=September 12, 2022 |title=Raiders claim Javelin Guidry, place Anthony Averett on IR |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/raiders-claim-javelin-guidry-place-anthony-averett-on-ir |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He was activated on October 22. He was placed back on injured reserve on November 29.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 29, 2022 |title=Raiders sign CB Tyler Hall to active roster; place CB Anthony Averett on injured reserve |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-cb-tyler-hall-to-active-roster-anthony-averett-ir-nfl-week-13-2022 |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On August 3, 2023, Averett signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2023 |title=49ers Sign CB Averett; Place CB Mitchell on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-cb-averett-place-cb-mitchell-on-injured-reserve |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve eight days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=49ers Sign DL Speaks; Place CB Averett on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-dl-speaks-place-cb-averett-on-injured-reserve |website=49ers.com |date=August 11, 2023 |access-date=August 11, 2023}}</ref> He was released on August 17.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2023-08-17 |title=49ers Release CB Anthony Averett From IR |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/49ers-release-cb-anthony-averett-from-ir/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On October 10, 2023, the [[Detroit Lions]] signed Averett to their [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reisman |first=Jeremy |date=October 10, 2023 |title=Detroit Lions sign veteran CB, TE to practice squad |url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2023/10/10/23911779/detroit-lions-sign-veteran-cb-te-practice-squad-anthony-averett-anthony-firkser |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=Pride Of Detroit |publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref> He was released on November 14, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=November 14, 2023 |title=Lions Announce Five Moves Including G Halapoulivaati Vaitai To IR |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/lions-announce-five-moves-including-g-halapoulivaati-vaitai-to-ir/ |access-date=November 14, 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On May 12, 2024, the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] signed Averett to a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=May 12, 2024 |title=Averett signed to one-year contract |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/averett-signed-to-one-year-contract |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He was released on August 20, and later re-signed to the practice squad.<ref name="a402">{{cite web | last=Varley | first=Teresa | title=Steelers make multiple roster moves | website=Steelers.com | date=2024-08-20 | url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-camp-roster-moves-x5059 | access-date=2024-10-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=August 29, 2024 |title=Steelers sign eight to practice squad |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-eight-to-practice-squad |access-date=2024-10-30 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He was released on October 28.

===Houston Texans===
On January 6, 2025, Averett was signed to the [[Houston Texans]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-6-2025)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-6-2025|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=January 6, 2025}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 21.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-21-2025)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-21-2025|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=January 21, 2025}}</ref> He was released by the Texans on March 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Houston Texans made a roster move|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-17-2025|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=March 17, 2025}}</ref>

In 2026, Averett joined the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]] in recruiting capacity.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Edmonds |first1=Javon |title=Syracuse football hires national champion, NFL vet to recruiting staff |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2026/06/syracuse-football-hires-national-champion-nfl-vet-to-recruiting-staff.html |access-date=3 June 2026 |work=[[Syracuse Post-Standard]]}}</ref>

'''Anfernee Jennings''' (born May 1, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and was selected in the third round of the [[2020 NFL draft]] by the [[New England Patriots]].

==Early life==
Jennings grew up in [[Dadeville, Alabama]], and attended Dadeville High School, where he played defensive end and tight end for the Tigers. He made 171 tackles with seven sacks in his junior season and was named honorable mention Super All-State by ''[[AL.com]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinor |first=Wesley |date=March 4, 2014 |title=Dadeville DE Anfernee Jennings hoping Auburn comes aboard after picking up Alabama offer (video) |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2014/03/dadeville_de_anfernee_jennings.html |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=[[AL.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bean |first=Josh |date=December 22, 2013 |title=Meet the 2013 AL.com Super All-State Football Team (photos) |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/meet-the-2013-alcom-super-all-state-football-team-photos/ |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=AL.com}}</ref> As a senior, Jennings was named first-team 4A All-State and the 4A Lineman of the Year after posting 170 tackles with 88 solo stops, 14 sacks, nine pass breakups and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hill |first=Jordan D. |date=October 13, 2019 |title=Local Legends: Dadeville's Anfernee Jennings leads Alabama defense in victory |work=[[Opelika-Auburn News]] |url=https://www.oanow.com/sports/high_school/_football/local-legends-dadeville-s-anfernee-jennings-leads-alabama-defense-in/article_e1af59be-b717-5e7d-831a-f42b0e3dde97.html |access-date=November 2, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hewitt |first=Trevor |date=January 14, 2015 |title=Jennings named 4A Lineman of the year in Alabama |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Jennings-named-4A-Lineman-of-the-year-in-Alabama-34746985/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227062037/https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Jennings-named-4A-Lineman-of-the-year-in-Alabama-34746985/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 27, 2024 |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref> Rated a four-star recruit, Jennings committed to play [[college football]] at Alabama over offers from Arkansas, Arizona State, Georgia, Mississippi State and Nebraska.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirkpatrick |first=Cliff |date=March 8, 2014 |title=Alabama football: Dadeville's Anfernee Jennings commits to Tide |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/2014/03/07/dadevilles-anfernee-jennings-commits-to-tide/6177569/ |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Jennings [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true freshman season as he moved from defensive end to the outside linebacker position. He played as a key reserve as a redshirt freshman, finishing the year with 19 tackles (two for loss) and three quarterback hurries.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Arbogast |first=Lizi |date=August 12, 2017 |title=Anfernee Jennings hopes to be starting LB for Alabama |work=[[Alexander City Outlook]] |url=https://www.alexcityoutlook.com/sports/dadeville/anfernee-jennings-hopes-to-be-starting-lb-for-alabama/article_c2fc2289-4e93-5c27-9bb3-a8317752c053.html |access-date=November 2, 2019}}</ref> Jennings became a starter during redshirt sophomore season and made 41 tackles, six for a loss, with one sack.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stuttles |first=Aaron |date=July 31, 2018 |title=Alabama counting on healthy Anfernee Jennings to elevate linebacking corps |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/452200/2018/07/31/anfernee-jennings-healthy-return-alabama-linebackers/ |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=The Athletic}}</ref> Jennings suffered what was initially diagnosed to be a PCL injury in the final minutes of the [[2018 Sugar Bowl]] against Clemson, causing him to miss the [[2018 College Football Playoff National Championship]] Game. The injury was re-evaluated and Jennings was found to have also damaged an artery and developed a blood clot in his leg.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zenitz |first=Mark |date=August 29, 2018 |title=How Alabama medical team and a fan saved a star player's leg |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2018/08/how_alabama_medical_team_and_a.html |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=AL.com}}</ref>

Jennings returned from his injury in time to begin his redshirt junior season. He finished the year with 51 tackles, including 14 for loss, 6.5 sacks, with an interception, a team-high 11 passes defended and two fumble recoveries (one of which was returned for his first career touchdown).<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Walsh |first=Christopher |date=August 28, 2019 |title=Sans Dylan Moses, Alabama will have to rely a lot more on players like Anfernee Jennings |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/sans-dylan-moses-alabama-will-have-to-rely-a-lot-more-on-players-like-anfernee-jennings-cBym-QyXwEOmkavKhE7GbQ/ |access-date=November 2, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]}}</ref> Jennings entered his redshirt senior season on the [[Chuck Bednarik Award]] and [[Butkus Award]] watchlists and was named pre-season All-SEC and a second-team pre-season All-American by the ''[[Sporting News]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Cliff |date=July 24, 2019 |title=Anfernee Jennings earns another watch list honor |url=https://www.alexcityoutlook.com/sports/anfernee-jennings-earns-another-watch-list-honor/article_9ccfe0fe-ae79-11e9-9b40-1fa01fd64e73.html |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=Alexander City Outlook}}</ref> Jennings had 83 tackles, 12.5 tackles for loss, 8.0 sacks, five pass breakups, one forced fumble and an interception and was named first-team All-SEC in his final season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Charlie |date=January 25, 2020 |title=Anfernee Jennings wants 'to show what I've got' in Senior Bowl |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Football-LB-Anfernee-Jennings-wants-to-show-what-Ive-got-in-2020-Reeses-Senior-Bowl-142702300/ |access-date=January 28, 2020 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref> Jennings finished his collegiate career with 194 tackles, 34.5 tackles for loss, 15.5 sacks, three forced fumbles, two interceptions and 20 passes defended in 54 games (38 starts).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Zach |date=April 27, 2020 |title=Analyzing Patriots' 2020 Draft Class By The Numbers: What We Can Learn |url=https://nesn.com/2020/04/analyzing-patriots-2020-draft-class-by-the-numbers-what-we-can-learn/ |access-date=April 29, 2020 |website=[[New England Sports Network|NESN.com]]}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
In the [[2020 NFL draft]], Jennings was drafted by the [[New England Patriots]] in the third round with the 87th overall pick.<ref>{{cite web | last=Clements | first=Devon | title=Patriots Select Alabama LB Anfernee Jennings in 3rd Round | website=Sports Illustrated | date=2020-04-25 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/patriots/gm-report/patriots-select-anfernee-jenning | access-date=2024-07-22}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in the season opener on September 13, 2020, against the [[2020 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]], playing nine snaps on defense in a 21–11 win.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Clements |first=Devon |date=September 16, 2020 |title=Analyzing Patriots' PFF Grades After Week 1 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/patriots/gm-report/2020-pff-grades-week-1-analysis |access-date=November 3, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]}}</ref> Jennings made his first career start on October 18, recording three tackles in an 18–12 loss to the [[2020 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Malley |first=Nick |date=October 23, 2020 |title=Dont'a Hightower still mentoring Patriots rookie LB Anfernee Jennings even after opting out of season |url=https://www.masslive.com/patriots/2020/10/donta-hightower-still-mentoring-patriots-rookie-lb-anfernee-jennings-even-after-opting-out-of-season.html |access-date=November 3, 2020 |website=[[MassLive]]}}</ref> He had 20 total tackles (ten solo) as a rookie in 14 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anfernee Jennings 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JennAn00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On August 31, 2021, Jennings was placed on [[injured reserve list|injured reserve]], ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach 53-Man Roster Limit; Acquire OL Yasir Durant in a Trade with Kansas City |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves-to-reach-53-man-roster-limit-acquire-ol-yasir-durant- |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

Jennings entered the 2022 season as a backup linebacker. He played in 16 games with three starts, recording 27 tackles, 1.5 sacks, two passes defensed, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anfernee Jennings 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JennAn00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he had 1.5 sacks, 66 total tackles (49 solo), and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anfernee Jennings 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JennAn00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 15, 2024, Jennings signed a three-year, $12 million contract extension with the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Patriots Announce Four Signings |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-announce-four-signings |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 2.5 sacks, 78 total tackles (43 solo), and one pass defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anfernee Jennings 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JennAn00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2025 season with two sacks, 26 tackles (15 solo), and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anfernee Jennings 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JennAn00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Jennings had a sack in both the Wild Card Round and the Divisional Round victories over the [[2025 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] and [[2025 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Los Angeles Chargers at New England Patriots - January 11th, 2026 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202601110nwe.htm |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round - Houston Texans at New England Patriots - January 18th, 2026 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202601180nwe.htm |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He had six total tackles in [[Super Bowl LX]], a 29–13 loss to the [[2025 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LX - Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots - February 8th, 2026 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202602080nwe.htm |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 11, 2026, Jennings was released by the Patriots.<ref>{{cite web |title=Patriots Trade C Garrett Bradbury to the Chicago Bears; Release WR Stefon Diggs, LB Anfernee Jennings and LB Jahlani Tavai |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-trade-c-garrett-bradbury-to-bears-announce-additional-roster-moves |website=patriots.com |access-date=12 March 2026}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Saints ===
On April 28, 2026, Jennings signed a one-year contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New Orleans Saints sign EDGE Anfernee Jennings and CB Martin Emerson Jr. |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/anfernee-jennings-edge-martin-emerson-jr-cornerback-saints-roster-moves-transactions-2026-nfl-season |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |access-date=29 April 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jennings's younger brother, Shawndarius "Shawn" Jennings, also played college football and originally played at Alabama with Anfernee before transferring to South Alabama. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Stephenson |first=Creg |date=June 21, 2017 |title=Alabama transfer Shawn Jennings lands at South Alabama |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2017/06/alabama_transfer_shawn_jenning.html |access-date=November 2, 2019 |website=AL.com}}</ref>

'''Andrew Barton Reid''' (born February 26, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for one game with the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerr/reid00400.html|title=Andy Reid Stats - Pro Football Archives|website=www.profootballarchives.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/ReidAn20.htm|title=Andy Reid Stats|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], rushing 160 times for 837 yards and five [[touchdown]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andy-reid-1.html|title=Andy Reid College Stats|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref>

==Biography==

Andy Reid was born February 26, 1954, in [[Hamilton, Ohio]]. He attended [[Hamilton High School (Hamilton, Ohio)|Robert A. Taft High School]] in that city. Reid played [[baseball]] and [[American football|football]] in high school, starring as a [[halfback (gridiron football)|halfback]] for the Tigers.

The son of former [[Georgia Bulldogs football|University of Georgia]] and [[Green Bay Packers]] player [[Floyd Reid|Floyd "Breezy" Reid]],<ref>Bill Moeller, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-journal-news-andy-reid-son-of-floyd/153167449/ "Bill's Board,"] ''Hamilton Journal News,'' Feb. 23, 1972. p. 28.</ref> Andy followed in his father's footsteps as a Georgia Bulldog. There he was a three year [[athletic letter|letterman]] and regular in the lineup during his junior and senior seasons.<ref name=MG77>Wilt Browning (ed.), ''Baltimore Colts 1977 Media Guide.'' Baltimore, MD: Baltimore Colts Football Club, 1977, p. 40.</ref> During his senior year he gained 468 yards on 83 carries — an impressive average of 5.6 yards per carry — and scored three touchdowns.<ref name=MG77 />

During his three years running the ball for the Bulldogs, Reid gained a total of 837 yards on 160 carries.<ref name=MG77 /> He appeared with his team in three consecutive post-season bowl games — the [[Cotton Bowl Classic|Cotton Bowl]], [[Tangerine Bowl]], and [[Peach Bowl]], respectively.<ref name=MG77 />

'''Anthony Bradford''' (born April 28, 2001)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bradford Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAn00.htm |access-date=July 2, 2023 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].

==Early life==
Bradford was born in [[Muskegon, Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bradford Stats, News, Bio |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4429211/anthony-bradford |access-date=July 2, 2023 'once-in-a-lifetime' Michigan offensive tackle who can dunk |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/meet-lsu-signee-anthony-bradford-the-once-in-a-lifetime-michigan-offensive-tackle-who-can/article_2c2fa3a6-353f-11e9-b267-f3278a6893f4.html Anthony Bradford preparing for the NFL Draft |url=https://localsportsjournal.com/2023/01/former-muskegon-big-red-anthony-bradford-declares-for-nfl-draft/ |access-date=July 2, 2023 |newspaper=Local Sports Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bradford |url=https://lsusports.net/sports/fb/roster/player/anthony-bradford/ |access-date=July 2, 2023 |website=[[LSU Tigers]]}}</ref> A consensus ==College career==
Bradford [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true [[freshman]] year in 2019, appearing in three games during [[2019 LSU Tigers football team|LSU's national championship season]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |last=Nettuno |first=Tyler |date=June 22, 2022 |title=LSU Tigers Snapshot Profile: No. 75 Anthony Bradford |url=https://lsutigerswire.usatoday.com/lists/lsu-football-anthony-bradford-offensive-line-roster-outlook-player-profile-2022/ |access-date=July 2, 2023 |website=LSU Tigers Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite magazine |date=March 24, 2023 |title=NFL Draft Profile: Anthony Bradford, Offensive Lineman, LSU Tigers |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/anthony-bradford |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 2, 2023}}</ref> The following season, he played seven games, with the majority of his playing time coming on [[special teams]].<ref name="auto2" /> He began 2021 with five starts through the first six games, before an injury ended his season.<ref name="auto2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Embody |first=Billy |date=October 25, 2021 |title=LSU OL Anthony Bradford unavailable rest of 2021 season |url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/BREAKING-LSU-OL-Anthony-Bradford-unavailable-rest-of-2021-season-Ed-Orgeron-injuries-173855392/ |access-date=July 2, 2023 |website=[[247Sports]]}}</ref>

Bradford was a key figure for the team in 2022, helping them go from 6–7 the prior year to 10–4, reaching the conference championship.<ref name="auto" /> He appeared in 13 games, 12 of which he started, only missing their match against [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]] for undisclosed reasons.<ref name="auto1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alexander |first=Wilson |date=September 19, 2022 |title=Anthony Bradford is available again, but he has to compete for his spot on LSU's line |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/lsu/anthony-bradford-is-available-again-but-he-has-to-compete-for-his-spot-on-lsus/article_94561de2-3861-11ed-8bcc-a76753380a09.html |access-date=July 2, 2023 |newspaper=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|Nola.com]]}}</ref> He appeared on a total of 899 snaps on the year and only allowed four [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], while being called for just two [[Penalty (gridiron football)|penalties]].<ref name="auto1" /> Bradford's primary position during his final year of college was at right guard, where he took 736 snaps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=April 29, 2023 |title=What to know about new Seahawks guard Anthony Bradford |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-take-guard-anthony-bradford-of-lsu-at-no-108-in-nfl-draft/ |access-date=July 2, 2023 |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Anfernee Chikezie Orji''' (born October 6, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]].

==Early life==
Orji grew up in [[Rockwall, Texas]] and attended [[Rockwall High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.texasfootball.com/article/2019/02/25/super-team-spotlight-rockwall-s-anfernee-orji?ref|title=Whataburger Super Team Spotlight: Rockwall's Anfernee Orji|work=[[Dave Campbell's Texas Football]]|date=February 25, 2019|access-date=April 27, 2023}}</ref> He was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Vanderbilt.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2018/07/07/rockwall-3-star-db-anfernee-orji-commits-to-join-his-brother-at-vanderbilt/|title=Rockwall 3-star DB Anfernee Orji commits to join his brother at Vanderbilt|work=[[Dallas Morning News]]|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=April 27, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Orji played in nine games and made six tackles during his freshman season at Vanderbilt.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/anfernee-orji-lb-vanderbilt-nfl-draft-scouting-report/|title=Anfernee Orji, LB, Vanderbilt: NFL Draft Scouting Report|first=Jason|last=Katz|website=ProFootballNetwork.com|date=April 9, 2023|access-date=April 27, 2023}}</ref> He recorded 66 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack, and two passes broken up during his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2021/05/03/vanderbilt-players-future-nfl-draft-2022/7401760002/|title=These Vanderbilt football players could get picked in future NFL Draft|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=May 3, 2021|access-date=April 27, 2023}}</ref> Orji led the Commodores with 93 tackles with 13 tackles for loss as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3282092/2022/05/08/vanderbilt-football-clark-lea-preview/|title=Vanderbilt football seeks progress in Year 2 under Clark Lea after ‘humble beginnings’|first=Joe|last=Rexrode|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 8, 2022|access-date=April 27, 2023}}</ref> He led the team in tackles for a second straight year as a senior with 106.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/vanderbilt/Article/Former-Vanderbilt-LB-Anfernee-Orji-boosts-NFL-Draft-stock-with-impressive-offseason-208672437/|title=Former Vanderbilt LB Anfernee Orji boosts NFL Draft stock with impressive offseason|first=Robbie|last=Weinstein|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=April 20, 2023|access-date=April 27, 2023}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
Orji signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] as an undrafted free agent on April 30, 2023.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-undrafted-free-agents-2023-nfl-draft|title=New Orleans Saints agree to terms with 11 undrafted free agents|website=neworleanssaints.com|date=April 30, 2023}}</ref> He was waived on August 29, and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-53-reductions-2023-nfl-season|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce practice squad additions|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-practice-squad-2023-nfl-season|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> Following the end of the regular season, the Saints signed Orji to a reserve/future contract on January 8, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-sign-11-to-reserve-future-contracts|title=New Orleans Saints sign 11 to reserve/future contracts|date=January 8, 2024|accessdate=January 9, 2024|work=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

On May 13, 2025, Orji was waived by the Saints.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/hunter-dekkers-quarterback-new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-update-may-13-2025 |website=neworleanssaints.com |access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On May 14, 2025, Orji was claimed off waivers by the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Titans Awarded LB Anfernee Orji, a Former Vanderbilt Star, Off Waivers From Saints |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-awarded-lb-anfernee-orji-a-former-vanderbilt-star-off-waivers-from-saints |website=tennesseetitans.com |access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref> He was waived on August 12 with an injury designation, having suffered a [[anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] during a team practice.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Titans Sign LBs Khaleke Hudson and Blake Lynch, while Waiving LB David Gbenda and Waiving/Injured LB Anfernee Orji |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-lbs-khaleke-hudson-and-blake-lynch-while-waiving-lb-david-gbenda-and-waiving-injured-lb-anfernee-orji |website=tennesseetitans.com |access-date=13 August 2025}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Orji has two brothers, [[Alex Orji|Alex]] and Alston.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2018 |title=Rivals.com - Alex Orji continuing family tradition of top prospects |url=https://n.rivals.com/news/alex-orji-continuing-family-tradition-of-top-prospects |access-date=January 12, 2024 |website=n.rivals.com}}</ref> Alex plays [[quarterback]] at [[UNLV Rebels football|UNLV]].<ref name=":0" /> Alston played linebacker at [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]] (2018–2021) and [[Campbell Fighting Camels football|Campbell]] (2022).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alston Orji Biography |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/player/bio/_/id/4362799/alston-orji |access-date=January 12, 2024 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

'''Anthony Ray Anderson''' (born October 24, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for one season with the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Grambling State Tigers football|Grambling State Tigers]]. He also played for the [[New Orleans Night]] and [[Orlando Predators]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL).

==Early life and college==
Anthony Ray Anderson was born on October 24, 1964, in [[Ruston, Louisiana]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/a/ande01400.html | title=Anthony Anderson | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Jonesboro-Hodge High School]] in [[Jackson Parish, Louisiana]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Grambling State Tigers football|Grambling State Tigers]] from 1983 to 1986.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Professional career==

Anderson was selected by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the tenth round, with the 256th overall pick, of the [[1987 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr"/> He officially signed with the team on July 28. He was released on August 29.<ref name="transactions"/> On September 23, 1987, he was re-signed by the Chargers during the [[1987 NFL players strike]].<ref name="transactions"/> Anderson played in three games for the Chargers, recording 0.5 sacks.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndeAn21.htm | title=Anthony Anderson | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He was released on October 19, 1987, after the strike ended.<ref name="transactions"/>

Anderson signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] on February 21, 1988.<ref name="transactions"/> He was later released on August 16, 1988.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/a/ande01400.html | title=Anthony Anderson NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref>

Anderson played in two games for the [[New Orleans Night]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) in 1991, recording seven solo tackles, three interceptions, and four pass breakups.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="Af"/> He also played three games for the AFL's [[Orlando Predators]] during the 1991 season, totaling three receptions for 31 yards and eight solo tackles.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="Af">{{cite web | url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/Anthony_Anderson-27/ | title=Anthony Anderson | publisher=Arenafan.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He played both offense and defense during his time in the AFL as the league played under [[ironman rules]]. Anderson was listed as a [[wide receiver]]/[[linebacker]] in the AFL.<ref name="Pfa"/><ref name="Af"/>

==Personal life==
Anderson's brothers [[Scotty Anderson]] and [[Stevie Anderson]] also played in the NFL.<ref name="Pfr"/>
